lesson: In next_job, the tenant that just ran must be excluded from selection if any other tenant has queued jobs, rejecting the initial proposal to only apply tenant fairness on priority ties.
why: A tenant submitting all jobs at top priority would still starve other tenants if back-to-back execution was only restricted during priority ties.
quote: If any other tenant has anything queued, the tenant that just ran is not eligible, full stop, whatever its priority.

lesson: In next_job, break priority ties among eligible jobs by choosing the shorter est_runtime first, resorting to earlier submitted_at only when runtimes are equal rather than using standard FIFO.
why: Simple FIFO ordering allowed quick jobs to get stuck behind massive jobs with the same priority.
quote: On a priority tie take the job with the shorter est_runtime first - that's what unblocks the quick jobs.
